text: In the language of differential forms, Green's, Stokes', and the Divergence theorems are all special cases of the single statement:
choices: integral over M of d(omega) = integral over M of omega
integral over M of d(omega) = integral over the boundary of M of omega
integral over the boundary of M of d(omega) = integral over M of omega
explanation: The Generalized Stokes' Theorem, integral over M of d(omega) = integral over the boundary of M of omega, unifies the classical integral theorems. The relation d^2 = 0 (not d(d(omega)) = omega) is what encodes curl(grad) = 0 and div(curl) = 0.
